title: Magnetic Properties of High-Entropy Alloy FeCoNiTi

recollection.starting_material: Guess: The paper likely started with elemental Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti in near-equimolar ratios to form a high-entropy alloy precursor.
recollection.intervention: Guess: The authors might have used techniques such as arc melting or induction melting to produce the FeCoNiTi alloy, followed by heat treatment or mechanical processing.
recollection.structure: Guess: The resulting material was probably a single-phase or multi-phase solid solution with a crystalline structure (e.g., FCC or BCC, or a mixture) typical of high-entropy alloys.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The high configurational entropy of mixing among the four principal elements could stabilize the solid-solution structure, influencing magnetic interactions among the Fe, Co, and Ni sites.
recollection.results: Guess: They may have reported moderate to high saturation magnetization (on the order of tens to hundreds of emu/g) along with a relatively high Curie temperature, consistent with Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys.

score.note: The recollection generically mentions arc melting and a possible multiphase/FCC structure, but does not identify rapid quenching, the composition-matched C14-dominant comparison alloy, or the specific fcc+C14 Laves microstructure. Its configurational-entropy mechanism does not match the reported antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling, phase-specific transitions, orbital/spin-canted effects, and domain-wall pinning. It provides none of the key measured values: 1084 K, 214 K, 168 K, or 667 Oe at 400 K.
